summary: Content Credentials record who made a piece of content and what was done to it, as signed statements bound to the bytes of the file. It is deployed rather than proposed: there is a conformance programme, a public list of conforming products, a published certificate policy and a curated list of trusted signing authorities. Two things a spatial computing group needs to know. First, no three-dimensional asset format appears anywhere in its list of supported formats, so a model cannot carry an embedded manifest at all; the byte-range binding works on any file, but the record has to travel beside the file as a separate manifest, and nothing keeps the two together. Second, the two pieces people most often credit to it are not in it: the verifiable credentials section and the training and data mining assertion were both removed from the core in version 2.0 of January 2024, and now live as separate specifications of another organisation. It records provenance; it does not enforce a licence, and its own principles say it passes no judgement on what it reports.

coverage.note: Statements about how an asset was made and changed are wrapped into a signed claim and tied to the asset by cryptographic hash.

coverage.note: Content Credentials travel with an asset. They say nothing about how a runtime blends its drawing with a camera view of the room.
C2PA records what a camera or tool did to an asset. It delivers no live face or body stream to an application.
Provenance data has no scene in it, so no walkable surface, bounds or arrival points.
Assertion labels are a registered vocabulary for describing an asset, not names for published units of world logic.

C2PA answers the interoperable half of this row and none of the rest. A receiving system can read a manifest, check the signature and the credential behind it, check each assertion, and show a person what has been asserted about the content — which is exactly the machinery a world would need to tell what an arriving asset has already been through. What C2PA never does is perform a review or name a reviewer: it carries claims, and whether a claim means the content was reviewed is left to whoever wrote the assertion.

coverage.note: No map of a place is declared by a provenance manifest, and no transform between maps.
An asset's credentials say where it was captured at most; they declare no area over which a service or dataset applies.
C2PA defines assertion labels, schema/version extension rules and backward handling of deprecated constructs; new provenance assertions can extend the model.
